prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the Z2 quantum spin Hall state and its first experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells, establishing time-reversal-protected topological insulators

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged from round 1: a single part for B013 to Kane, Mele and Molenkamp. After the full exchange, I see no member who contests the physics. Six of eight files prefer exactly this trio, and Kroll and Lindroth both name B013 as their first alternative, so the open questions are allocation and wording, not whether the field deserves recognition. The scientific case passes the tests I apply as an experimentalist. A general mechanism (spin-orbit coupling plus time-reversal symmetry giving a Z2 invariant and protected edge channels) was predicted. The decisive measurement (quantised edge conduction in HgTe wells) was made by one of the credited people. About eighteen years of independent reproduction by transport and photoemission across several material families give the long calibration-and-systematics track record that I ask for before I believe a result will last. It is the only shortlisted candidate against which no file raises a maturity objection. To answer the chair's own question on the 2016 prize in one sentence: the 2016 prize recognised topological phase transitions and the integer quantum Hall-type phases, while this part recognises symmetry-protected band topology in a time-reversal-invariant insulator, a distinct prediction with its own experiment and a materials field that grew from it. I will accept that sentence as sufficient and I ask those who raised the objection to say if they do not.
statement.case_against: The attribution remains the weak point and I do not want to hide it. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted the HgTe realisation that told Molenkamp where to look, and Zhang's death means that gap cannot be closed by adding a name. Hasan's ARPES work on 3D topological insulators is left out, so a citation ending on topological insulators as a class would overclaim for the three people named. I have therefore narrowed my citation to the Z2 quantum spin Hall state and its first observation, and I only use the broader class as a consequence, not as the credited achievement. A second topology prize after 2016 will also draw criticism, and part of my confidence rests on the committee being able to state the difference plainly. Finally, my own expertise is in astroparticle physics and detectors, so I am relying on the condensed-matter members on priority questions, and I recognise that some of the convergence on B013 follows from members reading each other's openings.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks B013 first, but is reported to have raised replacing Mele with Hasan so that the 3D ARPES discovery is recognised, and lists the BHZ omission and the 2016 prize as risks.
responses.response: I considered the swap again and I still cannot support it. Kane and Mele wrote the Z2 classification together, and the 2D quantum spin Hall prediction and its first observation form a closed story that your own configuration, which keeps Mele, also uses. Replacing Mele with Hasan would turn the citation into a mix of the 2D prediction and the 3D experiment, and Hasan would then be credited for a result whose theory is not credited. My view is that the 3D work is a real and large achievement but a separate strand, and I do not think it fits into a three-person limit alongside this one. If you do hold that Hasan should replace Molenkamp or Mele, I would like you to say which of the two you would drop and why, because Danielsson and I see no basis for dropping either.

responses.point: Kroll alone prefers B006 to Katori and Ye, arguing that the attribution is clean, that clock comparisons at the 10^-18 level are independently reproduced, and that it opens relativistic geodesy and dark-matter searches, while ranking B013 eighth only because it is outside his field.
responses.response: I agree with your reproducibility test, and the clock comparison is a closed loop between independent instruments, which is exactly the kind of evidence I trust. The two-name credit is much cleaner than anything else on the list apart from B013. That is why I put B006 as my first alternative. Where I come down differently is on maturity of the impact case: you accept that the redefinition of the second is still pending, and I would rather wait for it than reward a capability before it has become the standard. I also take your point that you ranked B013 low because it is outside your field. Would you accept B013 alone if the wording stays on the 2D quantum spin Hall effect, or do you see a reason it should be a second part with B006? I would not pair them, because a second part would mean four or five names, which the limit forbids, and Katori and Ye would be the only two.

responses.point: Lindroth prefers B002 for Bloch, Greiner and Zoller as a discovery about emergent many-body matter, but admits that five names are credited for three seats, that Jaksch is uncredited, and that she may overweight her own field.
responses.response: I think your discovery-versus-tool distinction is the right test, and I agree the Mott transition and the microscopes give a fair many-body result, with independent reproduction over twenty years. My concern is the one you raise yourself. Esslinger's Fermi-Hubbard work, Cirac's simulator ideas and Jaksch's original proposal all sit outside the three names, so a citation on the platform risks being diffuse and the split being disputed. For B013 the trio is already shared by six members. I would be glad to hear whether you could accept B013 alone, since you rank it first among your alternatives, and I did not treat your self-declared closeness to atomic physics as a reason to discount your argument.

responses.point: Mehlig reads B013 as a clean general mechanism and proposes the two theorists plus the first experimentalist, noting that the BHZ proposal is awkwardly outside the credited names and that the 2016 overlap needs an answer.
responses.response: I agree that the citation wording should do the work here. I have put the Z2 quantum spin Hall state and its first observation in HgTe quantum wells in the text, and I deliberately do not say that Kane and Mele predicted the HgTe effect, since BHZ did. On the 2016 question, I think it is a point for the citation and not an obstacle: the 2016 prize was for topological phase transitions and Hall-type phases, and this one is for band topology protected by time-reversal symmetry. Do you accept that formulation, and do you want the words time-reversal-protected in the final citation?

responses.point: Danielsson moved from B008 to B013, keeps Mele on the grounds that Kane and Mele cannot be split, and wants the citation to establish topological insulators as a new class of matter.
responses.response: I agree that Kane and Mele are a single theory contribution and I would not split them. On your wording, I would be cautious about ending on a new class of matter, because that reaches into Hasan's 3D branch and the credited people do not cover it. I have used a phrase that mentions topological insulators as the outcome of the quantum spin Hall prediction and observation, not as an independent achievement. I would also ask you to keep B008 in reserve with me: neither of us can lead with a single name, but the detection of the diffuse flux is secure, and if a defensible multi-person credit ever emerges it deserves a prize.

uncertainties: Whether Hasan's 3D topological insulator work can be treated as a separate achievement later, and whether leaving it out and the BHZ omission will be accepted as fair given that Zhang is deceased.
Whether the one-sentence distinction from the 2016 prize satisfies the members who raised it, since none has yet confirmed it is sufficient.
Whether Kroll and Lindroth will support B013 alone, and whether the observed convergence is robust or follows from members reading one another's openings.
statement.conflict_note: No change to my disclosure. My PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur collaborations and my KTH group are in astroparticle physics, and none of the credited people in B013, B006 or B025 is a known colleague or collaborator. I cannot be fully neutral on B008 because of my field and have not placed it in my preferred part. Condensed matter is outside my expertise, so I rely on colleagues for priority questions. As chair I have no conflict that requires recusal from B013.
